label: Fresnel Sheet
blurb: A flat plastic page magnifier held over the shot. A Fresnel lens is an ordinary lens cut into thin rings and pressed flat, so each ring is a little tilted facet that bends the light as the full curve would have. Inside the sheet the picture is enlarged, or turned upside down and shrunk once the shot sits beyond the focal length, and because every facet is flat the picture steps very slightly from ring to ring. The steep step on the back of each ring shows as a fine concentric line that grows stronger towards the edge, the rings catch the light in bright arcs on the side facing it, and the outer rings fringe with colour because each colour bends by its own amount. Distance moves the sheet towards or away from the shot, and a negative focal length makes a reducing sheet.
